hypothesis: Reusing each verified completed one-minute candle snapshot within its unchanged minute boundary in the V58 live poller can materially reduce shared-IP Hyperliquid REST weight and HTTP 429 evidence gaps without changing any provider output for identical completed-bar inputs.
decision: Request explicit approval to add the already-tested completed-minute candle cache to the live poller on a reconciled restart. Do not change the active process, strategy logic, routes, exits, sizing, leverage, stops, or poll cadence from this revision. Before cutover, add live-launch construction and all-route raw-versus-cached parity tests. After cutover, retain explicit missing-bar, route-parity, HTTP 429, runtime-fault, position, and protective-stop monitoring with no automatic promotion or rollback authority.
falsifier: Reject or roll back the candidate if any provider evaluation, intent, or withholding decision differs for identical completed-bar inputs, if a stale or missing completed bar is reused, if restart reconciliation changes position or owned-stop identity, or if the 500-cycle post-change diagnostic shows no material HTTP 429 reduction. The rate-limit diagnosis must also be updated if request instrumentation attributes the remaining 429s to a different source.
limitations: The per-IP request budget includes processes not yet instrumented with exact request-weight counters.
The venue documentation specifies additional candle-response weight per 60 items but the proposal uses only the documented base weight for its minimum savings estimate.
